$comment: Canonical structured source for get-connection-details. Draft v0.1. Prose in docs/sql-server-to-azure-migration-connectivity.md is written FROM this file, never the reverse: the recommend-migration-path skill arrived at canonical constants only after its prose existed, which left the same logic expressed twice. Connectivity is a closed, deterministic domain: a port is 3342 or it is not, so there is no middle tier of confidence. Every row is VERIFIED, meaning its quote was matched against the live Microsoft page, or it does not appear here at all and is listed in open_research instead. Agreement between research runs was explicitly rejected as evidence: two models agreeing usually means one shared training bias, and one run in this batch cited a page that returns 404. UNKNOWN when no quotable source was found. UNKNOWN rows are kept on purpose so gaps stay visible.

vocabulary.$comment: entra-default, entra-service-principal-certificate and entra-workload-identity were added during the merge. The original research vocabulary omitted them, yet entra-default is the mode both SqlClient and JDBC document most prominently. It is NOT a synonym for managed identity: it is a credential chain that also covers developer tooling and the CLI.

auth_support.quote: Virtual networks also enable you to join your Azure VMs to a domain. This is the only way to use Windows authentication to SQL Server. The other connection scenarios require SQL authentication with user names and passwords.

auth_support.$comment: Eliminates an entire class of connection string and is the first thing to check on a Warehouse credential error. Must NOT be generalised to fabric-sql-database, whose documentation is silent on the point.
Deliberately unknown. Silence in the docs is not a prohibition, and inferring from fabric-warehouse would be the single most likely source of a wrong answer here.
